items.title: What if owners of many homes paid more tax?
items.facts: MPs Elysa Chen & Shawn Loh, Parliament 6 Oct 2026 (suggestions, not policy; govt: beyond scope of Bill). Budget 2022: investment-home property tax 10-20% -> 12-36% by 2024. URA PPI +6.8% 2023, +3.9% 2024.
script: You are hoping for a bargain. Two MPs just suggested higher taxes on owners of many homes. Will they start selling cheap?
It's only a suggestion, not policy. But Singapore has seen this before.
In Budget 2022, tax on investment homes rose from up to 20%, to up to 36%.
Did owners dump their units? No. Private prices kept rising in 2023 and 2024.
Scenario one, most likely: owners hold, and pass the cost on through higher rents.
Scenario two: some sell slowly. Mostly smaller units. Small-unit buyers gain a little leverage.
Scenario three, least likely: everyone sells cheap at once. Owners of many homes can usually afford to wait.
So don't wait for a policy to hand you a bargain. Motivated sellers already exist, at MOP, at TOP and at slow-selling launches.
Which scenario do you think happens? Comment HOLD, SELL or RENT UP.

items.title: Seized luxury condos at auction. Bargain?
items.facts: ST 8 Oct 2026: >80 properties from $3B ML case; 26 auctioned 17 & 23 Sep, 4 sold ($16.28M), 22 withdrawn. Stacked: sold 1.3-7.1% below opening. Bloomberg: Martin Modern 2BR ~$2.08-2.12M close to previous prices. Next auction 28 Oct 2.30pm: 5 Nouvel 18 + 1 New Futura, freehold. Nouvel 18 guide $2,939-$3,558 psf; resales $2,772-$3,544 psf (Stacked). Claim backed by Penrose $1.8M vs $2.0-2.2M, Normanton Park $1.7M vs $2.1M. Do not name convicted individuals.
script: You are a buyer. You hear seized luxury condos are going to auction. You think: bargain.
These were seized in Singapore's $3 billion money laundering case. More than 80 properties are being sold.
In September, 26 went under the hammer. Only 4 sold. The rest were withdrawn.
The ones that sold went for just 1 to 7% below their opening price. Two Martin Modern units sold close to their previous prices.
Next, on 28 October: six freehold units near Orchard. Nouvel 18's guide prices run from about $2,900 to $3,600 psf.
Its recent resales? About $2,800 to $3,500 psf. Roughly the same.
So an auction doesn't mean cheap. Reserve prices are usually set close to valuation.
The real test never changes. Compare against what that project has already sold for.
With a dependable framework, we've found units $200,000 to $300,000 below market. No auction needed.

items.title: Two condos, same road. Which one rose faster?
items.source: Stacked Homes yearly avg psf; 99.co 2026 transactions
items.facts: A Treasure Trove avg psf 2021 $1,115 -> 2026 $1,640 (~47%); Watertown $1,393 -> $1,728 (~24%). 2021 quantum: TT 1,044sqft ~$1.2M, Watertown 1,109sqft ~$1.6M. Upfront 25%+BSD: ~$332K vs ~$445K. 2026: TT 1,044sqft $1.73-1.80M; Watertown 1,109sqft $2.409M (Feb 2026).
script: You're selling your HDB and you'll have about $400,000 in proceeds. Two condos face each other across a road in Punggol. Which one would rise faster?
One is integrated, sitting above the mall and the MRT. The other is a regular condo across the road.
In 2021, a 3-bedroom at the regular condo cost about $1.2 million. At the integrated one, about $1.6 million.
Cash and CPF upfront, including stamp duty: about $332,000 for the first, about $445,000 for the second.
With $400,000 from your flat, the first is within reach. The second isn't.
Since 2021, the regular condo's average price has risen about 47%. The integrated one, about 24%.
Why? More upgraders could afford the cheaper one, so it had more buyers.
We call it the affordability gap. Before you buy, ask who can afford to buy it from you.
Want to check the affordability gap for a condo you're eyeing? Comment GAP.

items.title: Your tenant is a 200 dollar company. Who pays when rent stops?
items.source: Mothership 9 Oct 2026; Yahoo/ST 12 Oct 2026 (District Court judgment, DJ Chiah Kok Khun)
items.facts: Lengkong Dua, Kembangan semi-D. Lease signed Apr 2026, 2 yrs from 1 May 2026, $7,500/mth. Deposit $15,000, only $7,500 paid. Only May rent paid. Tenant = company with $200 paid-up capital. Owners in 80s. Oct 2026 District Court: repossession, arrears $22,500+interest, double rent $15,000/mth from 15 Aug, costs $15,000+$2,031.98, commission refund $6,999.14, utilities $813.74, deposit balance; fixed sums total $55,114 (matches headtopics). Not vacated as of 12 Oct. Similar: Jalan Selamat 2019 (5+ months rent free, settled), Burnfoot Terrace 2024 (subsidiary, $1 capital, ~12 months rent free, suit ongoing). Civil only, no convictions. Do NOT name individual or companies. Infographic says High Court: wrong, it was District Court.
script: You own a landed home. A company offers you 7,500 dollars a month on a two year lease. A corporate tenant feels safe.
They pay half the deposit and the first month's rent. After that, nothing. The family living there doesn't move out.
This happened in Kembangan this year. The owners are a couple in their 80s, and they had to go to court to get their house back.
In October the court ruled for them: repossession, double rent until they leave, and more than 55,000 dollars in arrears and costs.
The catch is that the company had only 200 dollars in paid-up capital. Winning in court and actually getting paid are two very different things.
Court reports show the same pattern at two other landed homes nearby, in 2019 and 2024.
What we've found protects landlords: check the company's ACRA profile before you sign, ask the director for a personal guarantee, and collect the full deposit before you hand over the keys.

items.title: EC or condo? 4 things to check first
items.style: map (EC vs condo side by side)
items.facts: MSR 30% applies to new EC from developer (Redbrick; EdgeProp 8 May 2026). TDSR 55% all. Calc: $16K income, 4% stress, 30y: MSR loan ~$1,005K, TDSR ~$1,843K; $1.6M home LTV 75% = $1.2M; downpayment EC ~$595K vs condo $400K. New EC rules for sites tendered on/after 8 May 2026: MOP 10y (was 5), privatised 15y (was 10), DPS removed, 90% first-timer (EdgeProp; 99.co). EC 30-40% cheaper traditionally per Joel; v007 said condo gap >60% historically. Overlaps v007 (16 Oct) and v020; schedule apart.
script: You're deciding between an EC and a condo. Same budget. Which one should you pick?
Rules first. An EC is for Singaporean families within the income ceiling. A condo has no income limit.
The loan rules are different too. For a new EC, your mortgage can't take more than 30% of your income. For a condo, the limit is 55%, and that covers all your debts.
Say your household earns 16,000 dollars a month. For the EC, the bank can lend about 1 million. For a condo, up to about 1.8 million.
So on a 1.6 million dollar home, the EC needs about 600,000 dollars upfront. The condo needs just the minimum 25%, about 400,000.
Holding period: new ECs now have a 10 year minimum occupation period. A condo can be sold any time, with seller's stamp duty if you sell early.
Location: EC land costs less, so ECs usually sit further out. Condos tend to get the better spots.
That's why ECs were traditionally 30 to 40% cheaper, and why most EC owners have made money. They bought in lower.
But what if a new condo now costs about the same as an EC?
Torn between the two? Comment COMPARE and we'll run both on your income.
